cohort: The study included 77 nulliparous pregnant women at 41 weeks of gestation with a Bishop Score <=5.
finding: Ultrasound cervical length measurement was found to be a better independent predictor of cervical ripening success and vaginal delivery compared to the Bishop score in nulliparous women.
mod_finding: Cervical length was identified as a strong predictor of vaginal delivery, with a higher chance of vaginal delivery (90%) when initial cervical length was <32.5 mm.
